subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider \u2014 follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider — follow-up and next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — good to walk through Finlytics' streaming chat flow and the end-to-end latency constraints. Short recap + ask below so we can line up the perf test early next week.

Quick recap of what we heard:
- Primary target: end-to-end p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 500 ms for typical interactive chat requests (includes client network + provider time).
- Current traffic: roughly 180–220 req/s sustained during business hours; spikes to ~350 req/s in bursts.
- Concurrency: typical active concurrency ~40–60; peak ~120 during heavy campaigns.
- Streaming: partial-token streaming is used for UI responsiveness; client expects chunked responses every ~100–200ms once output starts.
- Throughput/latency sensitivity: some endpoints are latency-critical (chat UI), others can tolerate higher tail latency (bulk summarization).

Open questions we flagged for the perf test and qualification:
1) Can you confirm whether the p95/p99 numbers you quoted are measured end-to-end or just provider-side generation time?
2) Any IP/region constraints for traffic (we heard most traffic from US-East and EU-West)?
3) Do you have representative prompt sizes / token counts and average generated token lengths for chat messages?

Next steps (proposed):
- We'll run a hosted API perf test that mirrors your workload (concurrency profile + streaming).
- Aditya (cc'd) will draft the perf-run plan and required client changes.
- We request a small sample of current-provider logs/metrics (attachment or CSV) to baseline their p95/p99.
- Schedule: propose Monday 2026-10-19 10:00 AM PT for the perf run kickoff; if that doesn't work, suggest alternatives.

Attachments: redwood_latency-report.pdf (summary numbers from similar customers), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP).

Thanks — happy to adjust.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>

Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider — follow-up and next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: we measured the numbers you quoted end-to-end (client -> our proxy -> provider -> back to client) — so they include additional network hops.

Current provider baseline (last 30 days, peak periods):
- end-to-end p95: ~520 ms
- end-to-end p99: ~1,200 ms
- sustained throughput: ~200 req/s (spikes to 350+ for short bursts)
- concurrency: average active 50, peak observed 120
- streaming: yes — we rely on streaming for chat UI; partial chunking every ~150ms once model response starts.

I've attached a small CSV (current_provider_metrics.csv) with sample percentiles by hour. The big thing for us is preserving streaming behavior — we can't meaningfully change the UI to wait for a full response. Also procurement timeline: we are targeting a vendor selection decision by end of November; procurement and security sign-offs will take 3–4 weeks after technical approval.

Monday 10/19 at 10:00 AM PT works for a kickoff — we can run the perf test then. For the perf run, we'll need a short doc that lists the endpoints you're calling, the sample payloads, and which tests are streaming vs non-streaming. Also please confirm whether any client SDK changes are required to enable chunked streaming with Redwood's hosted API.

Thanks,
Samir Khan
VP Engineering, Finlytics
samir.khan@finlytics.com

Attachment: current_provider_metrics.csv (metrics sample)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@finlytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted API vs current provider — follow-up and next steps

Hi Samir — appreciate the CSV and the details. Quick technical notes ahead of the perf run: 

1) Baseline expectations (hosted API): for workloads we've seen with similar prompt/token distributions and streaming enabled, typical numbers are:
   - end-to-end p95: ~120–180 ms
   - end-to-end p99: ~280–350 ms
   These numbers assume client -> Redwood hosted API (US regions), no heavy WAN in the middle, and recommended concurrency/connection settings.

2) Streaming support: Redwood hosted API supports chunked/streaming responses (server-sent events / chunked HTTP). The client will receive the first token chunk as soon as the model starts and subsequent chunks at ~50–150ms intervals depending on tokenization and model. From the client perspective, no major SDK changes are required — just enable the streaming endpoint (we provide examples for our JS and native SDKs).

3) Concurrency & batching recommendations:
   - For low-latency chat flows, use smaller batch windows (25–50ms max) and prefer connection-level concurrency rather than large bulk batching.
   - Target active concurrency per worker ~40–60 for predictable p95; scale horizontally to handle peaks.

4) Network considerations: because your current p95/p99 includes network hops, we expect some delta if traffic routes through an intermediate proxy. For the perf run, aim to replicate the same routing or open a tunnel so we can measure provider-only contribution vs end-to-end.

5) Perf run plan: I'll prepare a short runbook with endpoints, sample payloads, streaming vs non-streaming tests, and a step-by-step checklist. We'll need a Finlytics contact (Samir or Priya) on the call to trigger traffic and a window where you can route traffic from your app to our hosted endpoint.

If you agree, we'll do the kickoff at Monday 10:00 AM PT and aim for 60–90 minutes to run baseline + a couple of burst scenarios.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
